page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DASv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 786 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No dedicated GPUs are included.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in multi-core stress-ng tests and CPU encryption, alongside strong results in PassMark CPU and memory evaluations. Single-core performance, measured via Geekbench and stress-ng, is rated as average to strong. Memory bandwidth tests show strong performance for cached small-block reads at 6005.62 GB/sec, though large-block uncached reads and writes drop to average levels. Database operations and Redis SET performance are strong, with Redis handling 89.06 million operations per second.

Given its high core count and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference. While multi-threaded decompression and ray tracing perform strongly, single-threaded tasks and large-block memory transfers operate at average speeds, representing a potential tradeoff for memory-bound sequential workloads. The hardware profile offers high resource density for general-purpose enterprise applications without the added cost of specialized GPU hardware.
description: Microsoft Azure D96as_v4 is a general-purpose server from the DASv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores. Operating at 3.525 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 384.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 786 GB local SSD, with support for Premium Storage. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and encryption capabilities, alongside strong database and Redis transaction speeds. However, single-core processing and large-block memory bandwidth remain average. The processor includes AVX, AES, and SHA instruction set extensions, enhancing cryptographic workloads. This resource-dense configuration is highly suitable for multi-threaded enterprise applications, database hosting, software compilation, and moderate LLM inference tasks.
